title: Capture of Philaenus spumarius and Cicadella viridis
author: Niels Appelman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8jdhui6

steps.title: Select appropriate field terrain
steps.instruction: Find a nearby area with short (under 30 cm) herb‑like plants, as both Philaenus spumarius and Cicadella viridis are polyphagous and will be present there.

steps.title: Sweep vegetation with insect net
steps.instruction: Swipe an insect net through the vegetation in one continuous motion, taking large steps while sweeping because the insects flee when the net is moved.

steps.title: Tap net at suspect insects
steps.instruction: Tap the net at insects that appear to be the target species; insects that immediately fly away are unlikely to be spittlebugs or leafhoppers, and note that both target insects have very short antennae.

steps.title: Capture insects with suction exhauster
steps.instruction: Use a suction exhauster (e.g., Vermandel insect‑vacuum) to draw the target insects from the net into a temporary storage tube.

substeps.instruction: Position the suction exhauster near the net.
Activate the exhauster to pull the insects into the chosen tube.

steps.title: Select and prepare storage tubes
steps.instruction: Choose storage tubes for temporary holding of captured insects.

substeps.instruction: Prefer 50 mL conical centrifuge tubes over the white‑capped 20 mL tubes recommended by Vermandel because the deeper tube prevents insects from crashing into the bottom and being damaged.
Ensure the interior of the tube stays dry; avoid any wetting, especially during rain, because surface‑tension droplets can trap and drown the insects.

steps.title: Invert tubes to let insects climb
steps.instruction: Place the temporary storage tube upside‑down so that captured insects can climb upward inside the tube.

steps.title: Secure tube sideward and cap
steps.instruction: Hold the tube sideways while removing the suction exhauster and screw the cap onto the tube; the sideward orientation markedly reduces the chance of escape.

substeps.instruction: Immediately screw the cap onto the tube while maintaining the sideward position.

steps.title: Transfer insects within two hours
steps.instruction: Within 2 hours of capture, move the insects from the temporary storage tubes into containers suitable for long‑term storage or directly into the experimental setup, because the insects are vulnerable to low humidity and prolonged starvation.
